newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rice market quiet, prices stable.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rice market quiet, prices stable.

text.p: Vietnam's export rice prices have remained largely unchanged this week as dealers await a delayed harvest in the Mekong Delta, traders said on Thursday.
"It's very quiet. There are no new shipments, just a few vessels in port here and they're old contracts from 1996," said a trader at a Ho Chi Minh City firm.
Five percent broken grade was quoted unchanged from last week at around $265-$270 per tonne FOB Saigon port, with lower grades quoted across a range to around $235-$245 for 25 percent broken.
Vessels currently in Saigon Port were bound for Iran, Iraq, Palau and Indonesia, although traders said the latter shipment amounted to just 450 tonnes.
Vietnam's next Mekong Delta rice harvest, which normally takes place from February to April, has been delayed by about a month because of recent heavy flooding.
State media recently reported government concerns that the total 1997 rice output would be lower than in 1996 as a result.
But dealers said on Thursday they expected total output for 1997 to be about the same as last year, when exports reached a record level of more than three million tonnes.
